candidate.perspective: Eligible private infrastructure developers seeking long-tenor risk-sharing capital for energy efficiency and cleaner industrial projects in Southeast and South Asia, rather than public-market investors.
candidate.structural_condition: Energy-efficiency and low-carbon industrial projects face financing, risk-allocation and long-tenor capital constraints; the World Bank/Japan DRIVE framework offers a new regional financing channel via a Singapore-initiated privately managed fund, but investment commitments and actual deployment must be distinguished.
candidate.delta: World Bank Group announced 15 October 2026 that the first DRIVE project is an investment in the Emerging Asia Infrastructure Credit Fund, targeting US$750 million in fund capital; IFC is investing up to US$50 million alongside JICA. The fund target is not a fully raised amount and IFC's 'up to' amount is not proof of full disbursement. Newly identified in 2 November discovery scan, not a new 2 November policy announcement.
candidate.mechanism: Risk sharing and concessional/development-finance participation may lower perceived project financing hurdles and crowd in private capital for energy-efficiency and lower-carbon infrastructure. Realized impact requires signed financing agreements, fund closings, eligibility, credit pricing, actual project disbursement and measured operational outputs.
catalysts: First/next fund close and audited paid-in capital versus US$750m target.
IFC/JICA actual disbursements, project-level debt terms and risk-sharing structure.
Named financed energy-efficiency or infrastructure projects with commissioning dates and measured energy savings.
Independent project performance and default/repayment disclosures.
candidate.invalidation: Fund fails to raise capital or reach financial close; IFC/JICA commitments are withdrawn or remain undisbursed; projects cannot obtain permits or secure grid access; pricing and project outputs do not improve versus comparable unfunded projects.
candidate.confidence: medium for official announcement; low for economic impact

evidence.name: World Bank Group, first DRIVE project and Emerging Asia Infrastructure Credit Fund financing announcement
IEA, Electricity 2026 grid bottlenecks and investment needs (context, not fund performance)

candidate.horizon: 2026–2028, conditional on financial closes and project deployment
candidate.evidence_stage: Announced institutional financing mechanism and capital target; no observed financing uplift, installed MW or energy-efficiency result
candidate.disclosure_limitations: US$750m is a target fund size, IFC US$50m is an upper commitment; neither should be treated as raised capital, disbursement, completed projects or economic impact. Source is the World Bank Group's own release; independent fund documentation and beneficiary data remain unavailable.
contrary_evidence: IEA grid queues indicate structural bottlenecks, but do not establish this fund's additionality or actual impact.
Development-finance participation can catalyze private investment, but displacement of other lenders and selection bias are not ruled out.
The first project was announced 15 October, so 2 November is a discovery date only, not a new event date.

research_note: Provisional cross-border capital-access candidate, separate from 1 Nov Korean equipment-export capacity, 28 Oct HBM4 capacity and 30 Oct BoJ ETF balance-sheet signals. Do not modify canonical Atlas or imply a country-level score.
